radioItems.displayValue: Array of Objects → Array of Values
radioItems.help:
Extracts one value from every object in the source array and returns the values as a flat array.

List one or more properties in Source Properties. The rows are read from top to bottom and rows that return undefined are skipped, so a property that is missing from an object falls back to the next row. When more than one row returns a value, Overwrite Existing Values under Additional Options decides which one wins.

Example
  • Source Array
    [{ prop1: "value1" }, { prop2: "value2" }]
  • Source Properties
    prop1
    prop2
  • Output
    [ "value1", "value2" ]

radioItems.displayValue: Array of Objects → Array of Objects
radioItems.help:
Picks the properties you choose from every object in the source array and builds a new array of objects.

Example
  • Source Array
    [{ prop1: "a", prop2: "b" }, { prop1: "c", prop2: "d" }]
  • Property Mapping
    prop2 → new_prop
  • Output
    [{ new_prop: "b" }, { new_prop: "d" }]

Combines several arrays into one array of objects. The arrays are zipped by position, so index 0 of every array becomes the first output object, index 1 the second, and so on.

Example
  • Array Mapping
    [ "a", "b" ] → row1
    [ "c", "d" ] → row2
  • Output
    [{ row1: "a", row2: "c" }, { row1: "b", row2: "d" }]

name: sourceArray
help:
The array to read from.

Reference a variable that returns a real array, for example {{DLV - ecommerce.items}}. Text, including a comma-separated list, is not split into an array.

If the value is not an array, or the array is empty, the variable returns undefined, or an empty array when Return an Empty Array Instead of Undefined is checked under Additional Options.

subParams.name: fallbackPropMap
subParams.help:
The properties to read from every object in the source array.

How the fallback works
The rows are read from top to bottom and rows that return undefined are skipped, as are rows that return null or NaN while Discard Undefined, Null and NaN Values is checked. Use a single row to read one property, or add more rows as fallbacks for the objects where the property above is missing. When more than one row returns a value, Overwrite Existing Values under Additional Options decides which row wins: the last one when checked (the default), the first one when unchecked.

Every object is handled on its own, so one object can be served by the first row while the next one falls back to a later row.

Use dots to walk into nested objects and numeric indexes to walk into nested arrays.

Example
  • Source Array
    [{ id_new: "a1" }, { legacy: { id: "b2" } }, { other: "x" }]
  • Source Properties
    id_new
    legacy.id
  • Output
    [ "a1", "b2" ]
The third object has none of the properties, so its value is undefined and is handled by Discard Undefined, Null and NaN Values under Additional Options.

subParams.name: convertArrValues
subParams.help:
Optionally converts every value before it is written to the output. Undefined, null and NaN values are never converted.
  • To Number / To Integer
    Converts numeric strings. To Integer truncates decimals. If a value cannot be converted the original value is kept.
  • To String
    Converts any other value to its string representation.
  • To Boolean
    The strings "true" and "false" in any casing become true and false, an empty string becomes false, anything else follows normal truthiness.

subParams.name: keepAllProps
subParams.help:
Copies every property of the source object into the output object first, then applies the Property Mapping below.

Leave unchecked to output only the properties you map.

A mapped property replaces a copied property with the same Output Property Name, unless Overwrite Existing Values is turned off under Additional Options. The source property itself is not removed, so mapping id_full to id keeps id_full in the output.

subParams.name: propMap
subParams.help:
Each row reads one property from every source object and writes it to the output object. Use dots to walk into nested objects.

Rows are applied from top to bottom, so the same Output Property Name can be used in several rows to build a fallback. Which row wins is controlled by Overwrite Existing Values under Additional Options.

Convert Value changes the type of the value: To Number, To Integer (decimals truncated), To String or To Boolean ("true" and "false" in any casing). A value that cannot be converted to a number is kept as it is, and undefined, null and NaN values are never converted.

The table can be left empty when Keep All Source Properties or Add Custom Properties is used. Entries in the source array that are not objects are skipped.

subParams.name: multiArrayMap
subParams.help:
Each row takes one array and writes its elements to a property of the output objects. The arrays are zipped by index, so values at the same position end up in the same object.

Arrays of different lengths are allowed. The output gets as many objects as the longest array, and objects beyond the end of a shorter array simply do not get that property. A row whose Source Array is not an array is skipped.

The same Output Property Name can be reused in several rows. Rows are applied from top to bottom and which value wins is controlled by Overwrite Existing Values under Additional Options.

Convert Value changes the type of each element: To Number, To Integer (decimals truncated), To String or To Boolean ("true" and "false" in any casing). A value that cannot be converted to a number is kept as it is, and undefined, null and NaN values are never converted.

name: addCustomProps
help:
Adds the same extra properties to every object in the output.

Custom properties are applied after the mapping above. They replace a mapped property with the same name, unless Overwrite Existing Values is turned off under Additional Options.

subParams.name: customPropMap
subParams.help:
Each row adds one property with the same value to every object in the output.

Values are evaluated and converted once and then copied into each object, so a referenced variable is resolved a single time. Convert Value works as in the mapping table above.

subParams.name: discardUndefined
subParams.checkboxText: Discard Undefined, Null and NaN Values
subParams.help:
Controls what happens when a value is undefined (for example a property that is missing from an object), null or NaN. Empty strings and zero are real values and are always kept.
  • Checked
    The property or array element is left out of the output, including properties copied by Keep All Source Properties and Custom Properties. A discarded value never wins over another row, so a fallback row can still fill the property in.
  • Unchecked
    The value is written as it is.

subParams.name: overwriteExisting
subParams.help:
Controls what happens when a value is written to an output property that already has one, for example when several mapping rows use the same Output Property Name, or when several Source Properties rows return a value for the same source object.
  • Checked
    The last value written wins.
  • Unchecked
    The first value written wins and is not replaced. A property whose value is undefined still counts as empty, so a later row can fill it in.
When unchecked, properties copied by Keep All Source Properties are kept as they are, and Custom Properties no longer replace a mapped value.

subParams.name: returnEmptyArray
subParams.checkboxText: Return an Empty Array Instead of Undefined
subParams.help:
Controls what the variable returns when there is nothing to output: no usable source array, no mapping rows, or every value discarded.
  • Checked
    An empty array.
  • Unchecked
    undefined.
